description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Vomiting / nausea history structure
points: Establish timing relative to meals, content (bilious, feculent, blood-stained), and associated abdominal pain — these localise the likely mechanism.
If the patient reports blood in the vomitus, prefer the dedicated CC_hematemesis pack — and first ask whether blood was coughed (hemoptysis) or vomited. Do not label the visit 'UGIB'.
Always screen for obstruction (inability to pass stool/gas, distention) and dehydration.
In women of reproductive age, pregnancy is a mandatory consideration.

modules.title: Obstruction pattern
points: Bilious/feculent vomiting with distension and inability to pass stool or gas suggests bowel obstruction.
Peritonism alongside vomiting raises concern for a surgical abdomen — do not manage with antiemetics alone.

Q000033.why_ask: Haematemesis/coffee-ground vomiting is a must-not-miss red flag in any vomiting history.
Q000033.think: Any blood-stained vomiting should trigger haemodynamic assessment before proceeding further.

Q000045.why_ask: Inability to pass stool or gas alongside vomiting is a core obstruction question.
listen_for: Complete obstipation vs reduced but present output
Q000045.think: Complete obstipation with vomiting strongly suggests mechanical obstruction.

Q000076.why_ask: Pregnancy must be excluded early in any woman of reproductive age presenting with vomiting.
Q000076.think: This changes both the differential and safe medication choices.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: GI bleed pathway
points: Assess haemodynamic stability before detailed chronic history.
Clarify volume and frequency of blood-stained vomiting.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: obstruction pathway
points: Correlate with distension, visible peristalsis, and prior abdominal surgery (adhesions).
